body:
Essentially, I assume that this change's purpose should be to solve this issue.

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/72484

However, this approach ignores default_fade, queue and breaks old behavior, so we need to do this in a more secure and robust way.

In any case, this change is not what the proposal is about and must be removed from the PR.

body: I think the name "default" is a bit too broad. If it were named something like "teleport_transition", the user would understand what it is without having to look at the tooltip or documentation.

Doing nothing here would make teleport_request a dead parameter, which seems wrong way. My feeling is that the correct way is doing what you are trying to do in [line 1065 - 1071](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102784/files#diff-9176faca3ecbebad6f340de9260278b31819bdfae318c1cd310a01c60229d0e7R1064-R1071) in this block.

So what should be done here is that when a transition_request is received, if there is already fading, it is discarded and replaced with a new teleport_transition.

---

By the way, if your intention in removing them is for perfect smoothing, then this implementation is not sufficient. 

As I have explained several times in some places, the current StateMachine only allows blending of two animations, transition_from and current. For perfect smoothing, fading should not be discarded and they should all be put into a queue array for processing, but this PR at this time does not seem to be aiming for such a queue implementation.

In this case, the safest approach would be to discard already existing fading and only process new transitions.

body: Teleport transition is a good name

> So what should be done here is that when a transition_request is received, if there is already fading, it is discarded and replaced with a new teleport_transition

I would actually prefer if the teleport_transition is appended to the end of the transition queue. In much the same way that explicitly defined transitions are already queued.

> For perfect smoothing, fading should not be discarded and they should all be put into a queue array for processing

Yes, the fact that it doesn't do this already was a mistake on my part.

The exact implementation might be outside of my skill set, but I would like to take another crack at it this week
This commit will be removed next time I update the branch

However, I think it is still necessary to add some kind of detailed distinction enum or additional bool flag internally for the teleport_request inside c++. This is because transitions from the start state and transitions by restart should not use `default_transition`.

Since playback by `start()` (i.e., immediate teleport) discards the currently playing transition here, this line would be required with some flags even if the flag `teleport_request` will be separated in detail. If you don't want to discard it, in conjunction with the comment above, just use `queue()` instead of `start()`.

body:
> Instead, the meaning of “teleport” should be narrowed - define "teleport" as "an immediate state change by start()". In contrast, a queued transition with no connection is a "default_transition".

Define "teleport" as "an immediate state change", either from start() or requested by the user. In order to allow users to replicate the previous teleport behavior, we would need to expose a "teleport" call for them. Even with a 0 duration transition, the `default_transition` won't skip an already in progress transition that has duration. Now, replicating this behavior would be considered a workaround even on master; but if there is a need for it, then it should be available if not strictly compatible.

body:
> Given the comments above, these should not be changed.

Correct. Alternatives are presented in the API section at the end of my large comment. Looking for feedback.
Yes, I agree with everything said here. Commit is not up to date with my most recent comment, as I wanted to understand a little better before I put another few hours into programming.

```suggestion
void AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback::travel(const StringName &p_state, bool p_reset_on_teleport) {
```

Since you pointed out the need for p_force_jump, I will reconsider and make some changes regarding my comments above.

> - Add queue_travel(String p_state)
>  - Concatenates the A* path from the last element of the travel_path array to p_state. If travel_path is empty, it is equivalent to travel().

> If travel_path is empty, it is equivalent to travel().

This should not be equivalent, but should be separated as follows:

If `travel_path` is empty:
- `queue_travel()` uses `default_transition` (means using `queue()`) for the first movement
- `travel()` uses `start()` for the first movement

This makes `p_reset_on_teleport` retain its meaning as an argument to be passed to `start()`. Also, `travel()` shoudn't have `p_force_jump`, instead of that, we should add `queue_travel()` to use `default_transition` with first movement of the travel (if the argument state and current state are not connected).

I'm totally down for adding a separate function (`jump`, perhaps) instead of a `force_jump` flag on the current `travel` call. However, I don't think `queue_travel` is the right name for it, as I would expect a function by that name to append a new series of travel request to the path as opposed to replacing all pending travel requests with a new shortest path to the requested state.

The current behavior of `force_jump` does queue a travel move after the current transition, but it doesn't have the same behavior as something like an `enqueue` or `push_back`. It still replaces the entire travel path, even though it retains any transition we are already in the middle of.

So, my suggestion is `start()` and `travel()` as functions to replace path, and `queue()` and `queue_travel()` as functions to add the path.

If your implementation of jump does not use travel_path, then the function name may be odd because it does not represent an actual behavior. However, as I suggested above, I have suggested the jump be determined by moving unconnected states within the travel_path (allowing arbitrary editing of the travel_path) rather than by the jump flag finally. I think implementing that is the most consistent way to avoid creating duplicate APIs.

My implementation only involves the suggestions relating to start() and travel(). Additional behavior such as queuing an additional transition at the end of the current travel_path are out of scope for this particular feature proposal.

The original implementation is as follows:

- `travel(State destination, bool reset_on_teleport)`
  - Use A* on explicitly provided transitions to find a path to the destination state.
  - If a path is available:
    - Delete the previous travel path and replace it with the new shortest path.
  - If no path is available:
    - Teleport to the destination state.

The current implementation is as follows:

- `travel(State destination, bool reset_on_teleport, bool force_jump)`
  - If the force_jump flag is set, skip to "no path is available".
  - Use A* on explicitly provided transitions to find a path to the destination state.
  - Delete the previous travel path.
  - If a path is available:
    - Assign the new path to `path`.
  - If no path is available:
    - Add the destination state directly to the path. (The `_find_next` function has been altered to provide the details of the default transition when an explicitly defined transition is not available.)

My preferred implementation is as follows:

// Note that the `reset_on_teleport` parameter is removed as we no longer teleport when we can't find a path

- `travel(State destination)`
  - Use A* on explicitly provided transitions to find a path to the destination state.
  - Delete the previous travel path.
  - If a path is available:
    - Assign the new path to `path`.
  - If no path is available:
    - Add the destination state directly to the path. (The `_find_next` function has been altered to provide the details of the default transition when an explicitly defined transition is not available.)

- `jump(State destination)`
  - Delete the previous travel path.
  - Add the destination state directly to the path. (The `_find_next` function has been altered to provide the details of the default transition when an explicitly defined transition is not available.)


My interpretation of your suggestions are as follows:

- `start(State destination)`
  - Delete the previous travel path.
  - Add the destination state directly to the path. (The `_find_next` function has been altered to provide the details of the default transition when an explicitly defined transition is not available.)

- `travel(State destination)`
  - Use A* on explicitly provided transitions to find a path to the destination state.
  - Delete the previous travel path.
  - If a path is available:
    -  Assign the new path to `path`.
  - If no path is available:
    - Add the destination state directly to the path. (The `_find_next` function has been altered to provide the details of the default transition when an explicitly defined transition is not available.)

- `queue(State destination)`
  - Add the destination state directly to the path. (The `_find_next` function has been altered to provide the details of the default transition when an explicitly defined transition is not available.)

- `queue_travel(State destination)`
  - Use A* on explicitly provided transitions to find a path to the destination state.
  - If a path is available:
    -  Append the new path to `path`.
  - If no path is available:
    - Append the destination state to `path`. (The `_find_next` function has been altered to provide the details of the default transition when an explicitly defined transition is not available.)

After re-reading your suggestions multiple times to try and get it in my brain properly, I'm pretty sure the only actual disagreement here is the naming convention? "travel" and "jump" vs "travel" and "start"

If you put the queue out of scope, we add an API with redundant arguments, but it will be difficult to remove those arguments when we add the queue later to keep compatibility, so I recommend that you add the queue and remove those arguments in this PR.

If that seems difficult for you, I would like to take over/salvage your work later by 4.5.

Which arguments are redundant? My main proposal has just one argument (the desired state). Actually, my main proposal already breaks compatibility. Should I retain the function signatures as best I can? Or should this be considered a breaking change?

I will not put the queue out of scope as long as there is no need for an additional feature proposal. The change is not trivial, but not out of reach either.

Do you take any issue with the vocabulary `travel`, `jump`, `queue_travel`, and `queue_jump`? I would not like to use the verb `start` as it would not be related to the internal `_start` and that caused me to misunderstand your suggestions

We do not explicitly use the word `jump`.

I assume you are indicating the behavior of using default_transiton between unconnected states. However, my suggestion is that they are automatically (without jump flag) processed if the unconnected states are queued, so all the user needs to do is the action of queuing the unconnected states.

> I assume you are indicating the behavior of using default_transiton between unconnected states. However, my suggestion is that they are automatically (without jump flag) processed if the unconnected states are queued, so all the user needs to do is the action of queuing the unconnected states.

Yes, that is the behavior I implemented in `travel`.

I also additionally implemented a way for the user to explicitly request the state machine to ignore existing connections, as a need for such behavior was brought to my attention [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98617#issuecomment-2464417352). I am aware that other solutions to this problem exist, but the use case is palpable.

Edit: changed link to a slightly more relevant entry in that thread.

If there is a connection to the queued state, default_transition is not used, but the existing connection's transition is used.

In other words, it is not always the case that a queued connection will jump. In other words, whether or not a queued state will jump depends on whether or not that state has a connection, not on the jump request, so only `queue()` is needed here, so `jump()` and `queue_jump()` are not needed.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98617#issuecomment-2464417352

If you want to do this, for example, if the current is `"A"` and there is a queue created by travel `["B", "C", "D", "E"]` and you want to jump to `"E"`, you just do like:
```
StateMachinePlayback.clear_travel_path()
StateMachinePlayback.queue("E")
```
Then, travel_path will be `["E"]` and if `"A"` and `"E"` are not connected, it will uses default_transition.

That's actually... exactly what queue_jump does. All of the behavior you're requesting is already present, I just called it `jump` and `queue_jump` instead of just `queue`. Are you sure the vocabulary is unacceptable? It seems like a provocative verb for a common use case.

Edit: To clarify, I'm not attached to the vocabulary, say the word and I'll make the change.

Edit 2:

> If there is a connection to the queued state, default_transition is not used, but the existing connection's transition is used.
> 
> In other words, it is not always the case that a queued connection will jump. In other words, whether or not a queued state will jump depends on whether or not that state has a connection, not on the jump request, so only queue() is needed here, so jump() and queue_jump() are not needed.

Missed this. Yes, this description matches the behavior. `jump` can be removed and `queue_jump` can be renamed to `queue`

If you understand my suggestion, the problem is that there are cases where a jump does not occur by `queue_jump()`. If there is a connection to the queued one it should not jump (it means using default_transition) but use the one's transition.

> If you understand my suggestion, the problem is that there are cases where a jump does not occur by queue_jump(). If there is a connection to the queued one it should not jump (it means using default_transition) but use the one's transition.

Yes, that is the behavior. What I have been *calling* `queue_jump` does exactly what your `queue` does. The fact that I felt the need to specify "using the state machine's default transition if a direct connection is not available" in the docs points to `queue` being the more accurate term here

I am also wondering about the difference between current `jump()` and `queue_jump()`. Perhaps `jump("State")` is synonymous with the following:

```
StateMachinePlayback.clear_travel_path()
StateMachinePlayback.queue("State")
```

and can be replaced with an implementation of `clear_travel_path()`?

There is actually already a public member `clear_path`, so I don't need to implement it again. I am actually rather fond of the `jump` function for the provocative verb, even if it's just bundling up `clear_path` and `queue` as you say.

Edit: You are right on the money btw

Edit 2: Technically they're not identical. `Jump` overwrites the travel path, so it prevents the need to clear it and *then* set it again. It's slightly more efficient, but I can't imagine this function being in a tight enough loop that this small of a difference matters

Well, then I think `jump()` should be removed. If it is really necessary, it can be written in 3 lines on the user's side. 

We should not unnecessarily add more terms. The only thing important to expose to the user here is the case information about where default_transition is used, and there is no need to define the name jump for that behavior.
